**REST:** Simple contract, standard HTTP caching, stateless. Client makes N requests per view → network overhead, high latency on slow connections. Client gets unused fields → over-fetching. Building new fields means versioning or new endpoints. Mature tooling, boring to scale.

**GraphQL:** Single request, client specifies fields → no over-fetching. Server parses + optimizes queries → resource-intensive (DB queries explode without careful batching/caching). HTTP caching doesn't apply — need custom logic. Steeper learning curve, but powerful for complex, highly-variable clients (mobile, third-party). Tooling still maturing.

**Verdict:** REST for simple, stable APIs and public third-party integrations (you can't control clients). GraphQL for internal tools, mobile apps with variable data needs, or heavy frontend complexity where the extra server cost buys real client-side wins. Don't pick GraphQL to avoid versioning alone — good REST design handles evolution.
